mainTopic: אביי challenges both רבה and רב נחמן on whether a בכור gets a double portion (פי שנים) of a debt that the heirs collected after their father's death.
overview: בני מערבא ruled that a בכור takes a double portion of a debt that the heirs collected after their father died. רבה tried to explain that ruling by limiting it to collected land, not money. רב נחמן explained it the opposite way, limiting it to collected money, not land. The background rule is that a בכור gets a double portion only of what the father actually held (מוחזק), not of what was only due to him (ראוי). אביי challenges each of them twice. First, each one's reason fits the other case just as well. Second, each one said something elsewhere that seems to contradict his distinction. רבה answers that these distinctions were only ways of explaining בני מערבא, and he and רב נחמן themselves do not hold that a בכור gets a double portion of a debt. The גמרא then begins to tell the full story of the grandmother (סבתא) case that was mentioned along the way.

steps.title: Money and land are the same: neither is what the father left
steps.stepSummary: Against רבה: the reason money gets no double portion applies equally to land.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is money different, so that the בכור gets no double portion of it? Because the father did not leave these exact coins. But land is the same: the father did not leave this exact land either!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's distinction. The reason רבה gives for money seems to apply to land just as much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה says the בכור gets no double share of collected money because those particular coins were never the father's. אביי answers that the debtor could have paid with any field, so the specific land collected was not the father's either. Both should therefore count as ראוי.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Used to challenge a distinction between two cases
Money, coins
Land
Their father left behind (as inheritance)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two opinions. רבה gives the בכור a double share of collected land but not of collected money. רב נחמן says the reverse.

phrases.english: What is different about money, that he does not get a double portion?
Because their father did not leave these specific coins.
Land too —
their father did not leave this specific land!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues אביי's challenge to רבה, which began right before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that collected money gets no double portion but collected land does.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה's own reason (these are not the father's coins) applies equally to land, since the father did not own this particular field either.

steps.title: רבה's own agreement with בני מערבא shows liened land is only ראוי
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge to רבה, from his own approval of the ruling of בני מערבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, aren't you the one who said that the reasoning of the people of the West is sensible, because if the great-grandmother had gone ahead and sold the property, her sale would be valid?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a second challenge to רבה. This time he uses something רבה himself said in another case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה agreed with בני מערבא that property is only ראוי when its owner could still sell it away. In the same way, the debtor could have sold his land before the orphans collected it. So by רבה's own logic that land is ראוי, and the בכור should not get a double portion.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, introducing an additional challenge
It is reasonable, it makes sense
The people of the West, the Sages of ארץ ישראל
Grandmother (here, the great-grandmother)
Her sale is a valid sale

phrases.english: And furthermore, aren't you the one who said:
The reasoning of the people of the West is sensible,
phrases.notes: Their case: a husband does not inherit, through his late wife, property that was only due to her from her great-grandmother.

phrases.english: for if the grandmother had gone ahead and sold it,
her sale would be a valid sale!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent challenge against רבה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that a בכור takes a double portion of collected land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה defined ראוי as property the current holder could still sell. The debtor could have sold the land, so it should be ראוי, and a בכור gets no double portion of ראוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a test for ראוי: if someone else could still sell the property away, the heir does not yet truly hold it.

steps.title: The same argument turned against רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: Against רב נחמן: the reason land gets no double portion applies equally to money.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב נחמן it is difficult. Why is land different, so that he gets no double portion? Because the father did not leave this exact land. But money is the same: the father did not leave these exact coins either!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי now turns to רב נחמן, who holds the reverse view, and runs the same argument the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן denies a double share of collected land because that field was never specifically the father's. אביי points out that the collected coins were not specifically the father's either. So money should also lose the double portion.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; a challenge

phrases.english: According to רב נחמן it is difficult:
What is different about land, that he does not get a double portion?
Because their father did not leave this specific land.
Money too —
their father did not leave these specific coins!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 1, now aimed at the opposite opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that collected land gets no double portion but collected money does.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason given for land (not the father's specific field) applies just as well to money.

steps.title: רב נחמן elsewhere treats liened land as already the creditor's
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge to רב נחמן, from a ruling he reported in the name of רבה בר אבוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, didn't רב נחמן say in the name of רבה בר אבוה: if orphans collected land for a debt owed to their father, the father's creditor can come back and collect it from them?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a second challenge to רב נחמן, using a ruling רב נחמן himself reported.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father's creditor can take that land from the orphans. This shows the father had a lien (שיעבוד) on it while he was alive, so it counted as his. If so, the land should be מוחזק, and the בכור should get a double portion of it. That contradicts רב נחמן's ruling here.

keyTerms.meaning: Orphans, the heirs
Collected (a debt)
Creditor
Comes back and collects it

steps.whatToRemember: אביי hits each opinion twice. First, its reason fits the other case just as well. Second, its owner's own statement elsewhere seems to contradict it. רבה's other statement makes the land look like ראוי. רב נחמן's other statement makes it look like מוחזק.

phrases.english: And furthermore, didn't רב נחמן say
in the name of רבה בר אבוה:
Orphans who collected land
for a debt owed to their father,
the creditor comes back and collects it from them!
phrases.notes: This is the father's own creditor, the person the father owed money to.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, הָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge against רב נחמן, matching the second challenge against רבה in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that a בכור gets no double portion of collected land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the father's creditor can seize that land, the father's lien already made it his. So it should count as מוחזק, which would give the בכור a double portion.

steps.title: רבה explains they were only giving the reason of בני מערבא
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers אביי: the challenges do not work against him or against רב נחמן. They were only explaining why בני מערבא ruled as they did, but they do not hold that way themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is not difficult for me, and it is not difficult for רב נחמן. We were saying the reason of בני מערבא, but we ourselves do not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers all of אביי's challenges at once. His land-versus-money ruling, and רב נחמן's opposite ruling, were only attempts to explain why בני מערבא give a בכור a double share of a collected debt. They themselves do not hold that view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה and רב נחמן each offered a way to make sense of בני מערבא's ruling: one by limiting it to collected land, the other to collected money. Since they themselves hold that a בכור gets no double portion of a debt at all, their own views elsewhere (the סבתא reasoning and the ruling of רבה בר אבוה) cannot contradict them. The flaws אביי found in steps 1 and 3 only weaken the explanation of בני מערבא, not their own position.

keyTerms.meaning: for me, according to my view
the people of the West, meaning the sages of ארץ ישראל
the reason, the reasoning behind a ruling
we do not hold this way

steps.whatToRemember: The land-versus-money rulings of רבה and רב נחמן were only explanations of the view of בני מערבא. In their own view, a בכור gets no double share of a collected debt, because it is ראוי.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבה is setting aside the סבתא statement or the ruling of רבה בר אבוה. Those are his and רב נחמן's real views. What he sets aside is the money-versus-land split, which was only an explanation of בני מערבא.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is not difficult for me,
phrases.notes: רבה is answering אביי, who raised the challenges.

phrases.english: and it is not difficult for רב נחמן;
we were saying the reason of the people of the West,
phrases.notes: He means: our land and money rulings only explained why the sages of ארץ ישראל give a בכור a double share of a debt.

phrases.english: but we ourselves do not hold that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא לְדִידִי קַשְׁיָא, וְלָא לְרַב נַחְמָן קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers all of אביי's challenges in steps 1 to 4 by explaining that the land and money distinctions were only explanations of בני מערבא's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the statements being used to challenge them only explained someone else's view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The land and money distinctions were רבה's and רב נחמן's own rulings, so they could be checked against their other statements.
steps.terutzMaskana: The land/money rulings only explained the view of בני מערבא that a בכור gets a double share of a collected debt. רבה and רב נחמן themselves hold that he does not, so neither the logical challenges nor the contradictions apply.

steps.title: What is the case of the grandmother?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the details of the grandmother case mentioned earlier and starts telling the story of a man who spoke to the people around him.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of the grandmother? There was a certain man who said to them:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the 'grandmother' case is and begins to tell its story. This is a setup line, and the rest of the story comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grandmother case had been mentioned only briefly before. Now the גמרא stops to explain it in full. Only the opening of the story appears here: a man began to say something to those around him.

keyTerms.meaning: what is it?
grandmother; here, the name of a known case
a certain one, a certain person

phrases.english: What is the case of the grandmother?
There was a certain man who said to them:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the double-portion debate and opens a full discussion of a case that was mentioned only briefly before.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The facts of the grandmother case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer begins here with a story about a certain man who spoke to those present, and the story continues in the next lines.
